newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland receives bids for firms Ostroleka, Romet.
newsitem.headline: Poland receives bids for firms Ostroleka, Romet.

text.p: The Polish treasury ministry has received several offers for bicycle maker Romet SA and more than one for meat firm Ostroleka SA, a ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.

"There have been several bids for Romet and more than one for Ostroleka," Maciej Chojnacki told Reuters on Tuesday, declining to give further details other than that the ministry would quickly find an investor for Ostroleka.
He said this was partly because a privatisation adviser would not be needed.
In March the ministry invited bids for no less than 10 percent and no more than 55 percent of Ostroleka's 1,350,000 shares. Sokolow has said was considering buying all the shares offered.
Ostroleka, which employs over 1,300 people, made a 3.3 million zloty net loss in 1996 and lost three million zlotys in 1995 on sales of 98.5 million zlotys and 93 million zlotys respectively.
Universal has said it seeks shares in Romet, of which 10 to 80 percent of shares are being offered. The firm employes 4,000 people.
